library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

Lindauer A, Snoeck E, Laveille C, et al. Exposure-Efficacy Analysis and
Dopamine D2 Receptor Occupancy in Adults with Schizophrenia after Treatment
with the Monthly Intramuscular Injectable Risperidone ISM. *J Clin Pharmacol*.
2025;65(3):350-360. [doi:10.1002/jcph.6152](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.6152)

The paper contributes two models to nlmixr2lib:

- `Lindauer_2025_risperidone_panss` -- the exposure-response model for the
  PANSS total score fitted to the Phase III PRISMA-3 trial, together with the
  dropout model that the authors used in their PANSS simulations
  (Supplemental Appendix S1).
- `Lindauer_2025_risperidone_oral` -- the oral risperidone /
  9-hydroxyrisperidone population PK model of Supplemental Appendix S2, which
  the authors combined with the Uchida 2011 Emax model of dopamine D2
  receptor occupancy (D2RO) to simulate the oral comparator of Figure S5.

The PANSS model takes the individual average steady-state active-moiety
concentration (risperidone + 9-hydroxyrisperidone, `CAV`) as an input. The
authors computed it from the Risperidone ISM population PK model of Laveille
2024 (Br J Clin Pharmacol 90:2256), which is not part of this paper. The same
upstream model drives the paper's Risperidone ISM D2RO simulations (Figures
3 to 6); those figures therefore cannot be reproduced here.

```{r load-models}
ui_panss <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Lindauer_2025_risperidone_panss"))
ui_oral <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Lindauer_2025_risperidone_oral"))
```

# Population

PRISMA-3 (NCT03160521) randomised adults with an acute exacerbation of
schizophrenia to intramuscular Risperidone ISM 75 mg, 100 mg or placebo on
days 1, 29 and 57, injected into the gluteal or deltoid muscle. The PANSS
analysis dataset held 383 patients (131 placebo, 127 at 75 mg, 125 at 100 mg)
and 2403 PANSS measurements taken at baseline and on days 1, 4, 8, 15, 29, 57
and 85. In the 390 patients summarised in Table 1, the median age was 41 years
(18-64), median weight 81.7 kg, median BMI 27.7 kg/m^2, 34.1% were female, the
median baseline PANSS was 95 (80-120), and 56.4% were enrolled in the USA and
43.6% in Ukraine.

The oral model of Appendix S2 fixes most parameters to Vermeulen 2007 and
re-estimates the shared central volume on sponsor data; the paper gives no
demographics for that dataset.

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| PANSS = BL (1 - PLA - DE) + DRIFT t | equation | Methods 'Exposure-efficacy (PK/PD) analysis'; control stream `IEFF` |
| PLA = PMAX (1 - exp(-(t/TD)^POW)) | equation | Methods; control stream `PLA` |
| DE = EMAX CAV / (EC50 + CAV) (1 - exp(-KT t)), KT = ln 2 / KTHL | equation | Methods; control stream `DE`, `KT` |
| DRIFT only in actively treated patients | `IF(DOSE.NE.0)` | Results; control stream `TVDRIFT` |
| BL (US) | 92.9 | Table 2 |
| TD | 8.32 day | Table 2 |
| PMAX | 0.117 | Table 2 |
| POW | 1.39 | Table 2 |
| EMAX | 0.0661 | Table 2 |
| EC50 | 4.6 ng/mL (fixed) | Table 2 |
| DRIFT | -0.0929 PANSS points/day | Table 2 |
| KTHL (gluteal) | 8.96 day | Table 2 |
| Ukraine on BL | +7.27% | Table 2 'COUNTRY~BL'; control stream `BLCOUNTRY` |
| Deltoid on KTHL | -69.1% | Table 2 'Inj.Site~KTHL'; control stream `KTHLSINJ` |
| Baseline PANSS on TD | +5.66% per point above 95 | Table 2 'BL~TD'; control stream `TDBLPANSS` |
| IIV TD, BL, KTHL (exponential) | 58.3%, 6.51%, 116% CV | Table 2 |
| IIV PMAX, EMAX, DRIFT (additive) | SD 0.12, 0.169, 0.134 | Table 2 |
| IIV correlations (15) | -0.827 to 0.5 | Table 2 'COR_' rows |
| Additive residual error | 4.78 PANSS points | Table 2 'addRUV' |
| Dropout hazard h = BHAZ exp(beta_PANSS PANSS + beta_USA USA) | equation | Appendix S1 (sign: see Assumptions) |
| BHAZ | 4.572e-5 1/day | Appendix S1 table |
| beta_PANSS, beta_USA | 0.049, 0.996 | Appendix S1 table |
| Oral structure (lag, zero-order input over D1 into the depot, KA split by FP) | diagram | Appendix S2 figure |
| F1, ALAG1, D1, KA | 1, 0.165 h, 0.458 h, 2.34 1/h | Appendix S2 table |
| FP (PM / IM / EM) | 0.0175 / 0.109 / 0.413 | Appendix S2 table |
| CLP, V2 = V4, V3, QP | 2.84 L/h, 118 L, 100 L, 3.65 L/h | Appendix S2 table |
| CLPM (PM / IM / EM) | 1.18 / 4.37 / 19.6 L/h | Appendix S2 table |
| CLM, V5, QM | 5.99 L/h, 91.8 L, 1.67 L/h | Appendix S2 table |
| IIV (ALAG1, D1, KA, FP, CLP, V2, V3, QP, CLPM, CLM, V5) | 41, 113, 149, 117 (logit SD), 184, 30, 54, 215, 33, 20, 81 % | Appendix S2 table |
| IOV (F1, D1, KA) | 46.5, 158, 108 % CV | Appendix S2 table |
| Mixture probabilities P(PM), P(IM) | 4.93%, 8.26% | Appendix S2 table |
| D2RO = Emax AM / (EC50 + AM) | Emax 100%, EC50 8.2 ng/mL | Methods 'Simulations of D2 Receptor Occupancy' |

# PANSS model: typical-value checks

The paper summarises the fitted model in three numbers: a maximal placebo
effect of -11.7% of baseline, a maximal drug effect of a further -6.6%, and a
total maximal reduction of -18.3%. The Discussion adds that the
concentration-dependent reduction (6.1 points) plus the drift over 84 days
(7.8 points) gives a placebo-adjusted change of 13.9 points, in line with the
13.0 and 13.3 points observed at 75 and 100 mg in PRISMA-3.

The typical patient below is a US patient with baseline PANSS 95 injected in
the gluteus. Risperidone ISM 100 mg gives a steady-state average active-moiety
concentration of about 38.6 ng/mL (Discussion, citing Walling 2021); 75 mg is
taken as dose-proportional (28.95 ng/mL).

```{r typical}
cav_arm <- c(Placebo = 0, `ISM 75 mg` = 38.6 * 75 / 100, `ISM 100 mg` = 38.6)

typ_ev <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  arm = names(cav_arm),
  time = c(0, seq(1, 84, by = 1), 1000)
) |>
  mutate(
    id = match(arm, names(cav_arm)),
    CAV = cav_arm[arm],
    PANSS_BL = 95,
    REGION_USA = 1,
    INJSITE_ARM = 0,
    evid = 0L
  )

typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui_panss), typ_ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  left_join(distinct(typ_ev, id, arm), by = "id") |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  mutate(cfb = panss - panss[time == 0], pct = 100 * cfb / panss[time == 0]) |>
  ungroup()

bl_typ <- typ$panss[typ$time == 0][1]
pla_inf <- typ$pct[typ$arm == "Placebo" & typ$time == 1000]
drug_inf <- 100 * typ$drug_eff[typ$arm == "ISM 100 mg" & typ$time == 1000]
d84 <- typ |>
  filter(time == 84) |>
  select(arm, cfb) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = cfb)
padj <- c(
  `ISM 75 mg` = d84$Placebo - d84$`ISM 75 mg`,
  `ISM 100 mg` = d84$Placebo - d84$`ISM 100 mg`
)

data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "Typical baseline PANSS (US)",
    "Maximal placebo effect (% of baseline)",
    "Maximal drug effect at 100 mg (% of baseline)",
    "Placebo-adjusted change at day 84, 75 mg (points)",
    "Placebo-adjusted change at day 84, 100 mg (points)"
  ),
  Model = signif(c(bl_typ, pla_inf, -drug_inf, padj), 3),
  Paper = c("92.9", "-11.7", "-6.61 at saturating CAV; -5.91 at 38.6 ng/mL", "13.0 (observed)", "13.3 (observed)")
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value summaries against the values printed in the Results and Discussion.")
```

```{r typical-gate}
stopifnot(
  abs(bl_typ - 92.9) < 1e-6,
  abs(pla_inf - (-11.7)) < 0.05,
  # 6.61% x CAV / (EC50 + CAV) at 38.6 ng/mL
  abs(-drug_inf - (-6.61 * 38.6 / (4.6 + 38.6))) < 0.01,
  abs(padj[["ISM 75 mg"]] - 13.0) / 13.0 < 0.10,
  abs(padj[["ISM 100 mg"]] - 13.3) / 13.3 < 0.10
)
```

The maximal drug effect at 38.6 ng/mL is 89% of `EMAX` because `EC50`
(4.6 ng/mL) is far below the active-moiety exposure of both doses, which is
why the authors found no difference between 75 and 100 mg.

```{r typical-plot, fig.cap = "Typical change from baseline in PANSS for a US patient with baseline 95 and a gluteal injection."}
typ |>
  filter(time <= 84) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, cfb, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time since first injection (day)", y = "PANSS change from baseline", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# PANSS model: virtual PRISMA-3 cohort

The virtual cohort has 200 patients per arm in each country (USA and
Ukraine). Baseline PANSS is drawn from a normal distribution with the Table 1
mean (96.3) and coefficient of variation (8.3%), truncated to the 80-120 entry
range. All patients receive gluteal injections except in the injection-site
comparison below. `CAV` is the arm's typical value; the paper used each
patient's post hoc CL/F, whose distribution it does not report.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20250325)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250325)
n_per <- 200L
visits <- c(0, 4, 8, 15, 29, 57, 85)

make_cohort <- function(arm, region_usa, injsite_arm, id_offset) {
  bl <- round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_per, 96.3, 0.083 * 96.3), 80), 120))
  tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_per),
    arm = arm,
    country = ifelse(region_usa == 1, "USA", "Ukraine"),
    site = ifelse(injsite_arm == 1, "Deltoid", "Gluteus"),
    CAV = unname(cav_arm[arm]),
    PANSS_BL = bl,
    REGION_USA = region_usa,
    INJSITE_ARM = injsite_arm,
    u_drop = runif(n_per)
  )
}

design <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  arm = names(cav_arm), region_usa = c(1, 0), injsite_arm = 0
) |>
  bind_rows(tibble::tibble(arm = names(cav_arm), region_usa = 1, injsite_arm = 1))
subj <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(design)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(design$arm[i], design$region_usa[i], design$injsite_arm[i], (i - 1L) * n_per)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(subj$id))

ev <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = subj$id, time = sort(unique(c(0:85, visits)))) |>
  left_join(select(subj, id, CAV, PANSS_BL, REGION_USA, INJSITE_ARM), by = "id") |>
  mutate(evid = 0L)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_panss, ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  left_join(select(subj, id, arm, country, site, u_drop), by = "id")
```

The dropout model of Appendix S1 gives each patient a survival curve
`sur(t)`. A patient drops out at the first time `sur(t)` falls below a uniform
random number; visits after dropout carry the last observed PANSS forward
(LOCF), as in the paper's simulations.

```{r dropout}
drop_time <- sim |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(t_drop = suppressWarnings(min(time[sur < u_drop[1]])), .groups = "drop")

vis <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% visits) |>
  left_join(drop_time, by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(
    y = ifelse(time < t_drop, sim, NA_real_),
    y_locf = y
  ) |>
  tidyr::fill(y_locf, .direction = "down") |>
  mutate(cfb = y_locf - y_locf[time == 0]) |>
  ungroup()

vis |>
  filter(site == "Gluteus") |>
  group_by(arm, country) |>
  summarise(`Dropped out by day 85 (%)` = round(100 * mean(is.na(y[time == 85])), 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated dropout by day 85 (gluteal cohorts).")
```

Patients enrolled in the USA, and those with higher PANSS, drop out faster,
which is why placebo patients drop out more often than actively treated ones.

## Replicates Figure 1 (VPC by country and treatment)

```{r fig1, fig.cap = "Simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of PANSS without dropout, by country and arm. Compare with Figure 1 of Lindauer 2025."}
vpc <- sim |>
  filter(site == "Gluteus", time %in% visits) |>
  group_by(arm, country, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "darkseagreen", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "darkred", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_grid(country ~ factor(arm, levels = names(cav_arm))) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "PANSS") +
  theme_bw()
```

The observed medians in Figure 1 start near 100 in Ukraine and near 92 in the
USA and, by day 85, fall to roughly 87 (placebo), 71 (75 mg) and 67 (100 mg)
in Ukraine and 79, 66 and 69 in the USA (read from the figure). The model's
medians are compared below; Figure 1's observed medians are of the patients
still in the study, so they are not adjusted for dropout.

```{r fig1-table}
vpc |>
  filter(time %in% c(0, 85)) |>
  mutate(time = paste("Day", time)) |>
  select(arm, country, time, p50) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = p50) |>
  mutate(`Figure 1 day 85 (approx.)` = c(79, 87, 66, 71, 69, 67)[match(
    paste(arm, country),
    c(
      "Placebo USA", "Placebo Ukraine", "ISM 75 mg USA", "ISM 75 mg Ukraine",
      "ISM 100 mg USA", "ISM 100 mg Ukraine"
    )
  )]) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated median PANSS against the observed medians read from Figure 1.")
```

## Replicates Figure 2 (injection site, US patients)

```{r fig2, fig.cap = "Median and 90% prediction interval of the PANSS change from baseline over the first 28 days in US patients by injection site, with dropout and LOCF. Compare with Figure 2 of Lindauer 2025."}
fig2 <- vis |>
  filter(country == "USA", time <= 29) |>
  group_by(arm, site, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(cfb, 0.05), p50 = median(cfb), p95 = quantile(cfb, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(fig2, aes(time, p50, colour = site, fill = site)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(arm, levels = names(cav_arm))) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "PANSS change from baseline", colour = "Injection site", fill = "Injection site") +
  theme_bw()
```

In Figure 2 the median change at day 28 is about -10.5 points for placebo and
about -18 points for both doses, with the deltoid curves slightly ahead of
the gluteal ones in the first two weeks.

```{r fig2-gate}
fig2_d29 <- fig2 |>
  filter(time == 29, site == "Gluteus") |>
  mutate(paper = c(Placebo = -10.5, `ISM 75 mg` = -18, `ISM 100 mg` = -17.5)[arm])
knitr::kable(
  fig2_d29 |>
    select(arm, p50, paper) |>
    mutate(p50 = round(p50, 1)) |>
    dplyr::rename(Arm = arm, `Simulated median` = p50, `Figure 2 (approx.)` = paper),
  caption = "Median PANSS change from baseline at the day-29 visit, US gluteal patients."
)
# The medians are read from the figure (about +/-1 point) and a 200-patient
# median moves by about 1 point between cohort draws.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig2_d29$p50 - fig2_d29$paper) < 4))
```

## D2 receptor occupancy at the Risperidone ISM average concentration

The Uchida 2011 Emax model (Emax 100%, EC50 8.2 ng/mL), evaluated at the
reported steady-state average active-moiety concentration of 38.6 ng/mL after
100 mg, gives an average occupancy of
`r round(100 * 38.6 / (8.2 + 38.6), 1)`%. The full time course after each
injection requires the Laveille 2024 Risperidone ISM population PK model.

# Oral risperidone PK and D2 receptor occupancy

## Replicates Figure S5

Figure S5 shows the active-moiety concentration and D2RO over the first week
of 3 and 4 mg once-daily oral risperidone in 1000 simulated patients. Here
200 patients per dose are simulated, with CYP2D6 phenotype drawn from the
mixture probabilities (4.93% poor, 8.26% intermediate, 86.81% extensive
metabolizers) and a new inter-occasion draw for every dose (`OCC` = dose
number).

```{r oral-sim}
set.seed(20250326)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250326)
n_oral <- 200L
obs_t <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 168, by = 1), seq(0, 168, by = 0.25)[seq(0, 168, by = 0.25) < 6])))

oral_subj <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose = c(3, 4), k = seq_len(n_oral)) |>
  mutate(
    id = seq_len(n()),
    treatment = paste(dose, "mg QD"),
    phen = sample(c("PM", "IM", "EM"), n(), replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.0493, 0.0826, 0.8681)),
    CYP2D6_PM = as.integer(phen == "PM"),
    CYP2D6_IM = as.integer(phen == "IM")
  )

oral_ev <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = oral_subj$id, time = seq(0, 144, by = 24)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = oral_subj$id, time = obs_t) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
) |>
  left_join(select(oral_subj, id, dose, treatment, CYP2D6_PM, CYP2D6_IM), by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, dose, 0),
    OCC = pmin(floor(time / 24) + 1, 7)
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

oral_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  ui_oral, oral_ev,
  returnType = "data.frame", keep = "treatment"
)

# rxode2 draws the occasion effects per subject and occasion only when some
# subject has two or more `OCC` levels, as here (levels 1 to 7 for every
# subject). When every subject has exactly one, it treats `OCC` as a level above
# the subject and all subjects on an occasion share one draw. Asserting the
# distinct draws per occasion makes the render fail instead of sharing silently.
nlmixr2lib:::assertDrawsPerLevel(
  oral_sim,
  eta = c("etaiov_fdepot", "etaiov_d1", "etaiov_ka"),
  by = "OCC",
  n = 2L * n_oral
)
stopifnot(length(unique(oral_sim$OCC)) == 7L)
```

```{r figS5, fig.cap = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles of the active-moiety concentration (orange) and D2RO (blue) over the first week of oral risperidone. The dashed line marks 65% D2RO. Compare with Figure S5 of Lindauer 2025."}
s5 <- oral_sim |>
  select(id, time, treatment, AM, D2RO) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(AM, D2RO), names_to = "output") |>
  group_by(treatment, output, time) |>
  summarise(p05 = quantile(value, 0.05), p50 = median(value), p95 = quantile(value, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(s5, aes(time, p50, colour = output, fill = output)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 65, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, ncol = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(AM = "darkorange", D2RO = "navy"), labels = c("Active moiety (ng/mL)", "D2RO (%)")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(AM = "darkorange", D2RO = "navy"), labels = c("Active moiety (ng/mL)", "D2RO (%)")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 168, by = 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL) or D2RO (%)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

## PKNCA of the active moiety

PKNCA is run on the active moiety for the first dosing interval and for the
seventh (steady-state) interval, grouped by dose.

```{r pknca}
conc <- oral_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(AM)) |>
  select(id, time, treatment, AM) |>
  dplyr::rename(Cc = AM)
doses <- oral_ev |>
  filter(evid == 1L) |>
  select(id, time, treatment, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 144), end = c(24, 168),
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, cav = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "cmin", "cav")) |>
  mutate(interval = ifelse(start == 0, "Dose 1", "Dose 7")) |>
  group_by(treatment, interval, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Treatment = treatment, Interval = interval, `Cmax (ng/mL)` = cmax,
    `Tmax (h)` = tmax, `Cmin (ng/mL)` = cmin, `Cav (ng/mL)` = cav
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median active-moiety NCA by dose and dosing interval.")
```

The paper prints no NCA table for the oral comparator. Its median curves in
Figure S5, read from the figure, give the reference below: first-dose peaks of
about 19.5 and 25.5 ng/mL and seventh-dose peaks of about 38 and 49.5 ng/mL,
with trough values of about 19 and 25 ng/mL at 168 h. The comparison pools
the per-subject values by their median.

```{r nca-compare}
dose7 <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(start == 144, PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin"))
published <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("3 mg QD", "4 mg QD"),
  cmax = c(38, 49.5),
  cmin = c(19, 25)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = dose7,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", cmin = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Seventh-dose median active-moiety Cmax and Cmin against the medians read from Figure S5. * marks rows differing by more than 20%.")
```

```{r oral-gate}
first_peak <- s5 |>
  filter(output == "AM", time <= 24) |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(peak = max(p50), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(paper = c(`3 mg QD` = 19.5, `4 mg QD` = 25.5)[treatment])
# The PK is linear in dose, so the two arms differ only by a scale factor.
# Pooling their dose-normalised first-dose curves puts 400 subjects behind each
# median; the median peak of one 200-subject arm depends on a few draws of the
# absorption parameters (149% CV on KA, 158% IOV on D1).
dose_by_id <- select(oral_subj, id, dose)
pooled_curve <- oral_sim |>
  filter(time <= 24) |>
  left_join(dose_by_id, by = "id") |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(p50 = median(AM / dose), .groups = "drop")
pooled_peak <- max(pooled_curve$p50)
pooled_tmax <- pooled_curve$time[which.max(pooled_curve$p50)]
# D2RO increases with the active-moiety concentration, so the median D2RO at a
# time is the D2RO of the median concentration. It is evaluated at the pooled
# dose-normalised peak scaled to each dose, which rests on the 400 pooled
# subjects. The Figure S5 3 mg peak (19.5 ng/mL) is close to the 15.2 ng/mL that
# gives 65% D2RO (Emax 100%, EC50 8.2 ng/mL), so the gate below is a floor of 55%
# (10.0 ng/mL), not a test against 65%.
d2ro_at_peak <- tibble(treatment = c("3 mg QD", "4 mg QD"), dose = c(3, 4)) |>
  mutate(
    am_peak = dose * pooled_peak,
    d2ro_peak = ui_oral$theta[["emax"]] * am_peak / (exp(ui_oral$theta[["lec50"]]) + am_peak)
  )
knitr::kable(
  first_peak |>
    left_join(d2ro_at_peak, by = "treatment") |>
    transmute(
      Treatment = treatment,
      `Simulated first-dose median peak (ng/mL)` = round(peak, 1),
      `Figure S5 (approx.)` = paper,
      `Median D2RO at the pooled first-dose peak (%)` = round(d2ro_peak, 1)
    ),
  caption = "First-dose median active-moiety peak per arm, and the median D2RO at the pooled dose-normalised peak scaled to each dose."
)
paper_per_mg <- mean(c(19.5 / 3, 25.5 / 4))
cat(sprintf(
  "Pooled dose-normalised first-dose median peak: %.2f ng/mL per mg (Figure S5: %.2f) at %.2f h\n",
  pooled_peak, paper_per_mg, pooled_tmax
))
# Average concentration over the seventh dosing interval (144-168 h): the AUC of
# the pooled dose-normalised median curve, trapezoidal on the hourly grid. For
# any profile the average over an interval lies between its minimum and maximum,
# so a model with the published exposure has an AUC between 24 h times the
# seventh-dose trough per mg and 24 h times the seventh-dose peak per mg read
# from Figure S5 (the larger of the two arms' trough per mg and the smaller of
# their peak per mg).
dose7_curve <- oral_sim |>
  filter(time >= 144, time <= 168) |>
  left_join(dose_by_id, by = "id") |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(p50 = median(AM / dose), .groups = "drop")
auc7_per_mg <- with(
  dose7_curve,
  sum(diff(time) * (head(p50, -1) + tail(p50, -1)) / 2)
)
published_per_mg <- published |>
  mutate(dose = as.numeric(sub(" mg QD", "", treatment)))
auc7_lower <- 24 * max(published_per_mg$cmin / published_per_mg$dose)
auc7_upper <- 24 * min(published_per_mg$cmax / published_per_mg$dose)
cat(sprintf(
  "Seventh-interval AUC per mg: %.0f ng*h/mL (Figure S5 trough-to-peak envelope %.0f to %.0f)\n",
  auc7_per_mg, auc7_lower, auc7_upper
))
stopifnot(
  # The pooled peak is set by absorption (KA, lag, IOV on D1), so the draw moves
  # it by up to about a quarter, while a mis-transcribed dose or unit scales it.
  # It is only weakly sensitive to clearance (tripling both clearances lowers it
  # by about a tenth of the Figure S5 value), so the AUC check below carries
  # clearance.
  abs(pooled_peak - paper_per_mg) / paper_per_mg < 0.30,
  # A KA four times too small moves the pooled median peak time to 4.75-6 h; the
  # draw moves it within 2.25-3 h.
  pooled_tmax >= 1, pooled_tmax <= 4,
  # A mis-transcribed EC50 or Emax moves the occupancy at the peak by tens of
  # points; the draw by a few.
  all(d2ro_at_peak$d2ro_peak >= 55),
  # Clearance: the seventh-interval AUC falls to about a third when both
  # clearances are tripled and rises about 2.6 times when they are divided by
  # three, so a threefold error either way leaves the envelope (which spans a
  # factor of 1.95), while the draw moves the AUC by under 10%.
  auc7_per_mg >= auc7_lower, auc7_per_mg <= auc7_upper
)
```

The first-dose peak, pooled over both doses after dose normalisation, is
compared with Figure S5 within a 30% bound that allows for the absorption draw
(the per-mg values are printed above), and the median D2RO at that peak is close
to the 65% line of the figure for 3 mg and above it for 4 mg. The seventh-interval
AUC per mg, pooled the same way, lies between the figure's trough and peak per
mg (the average over an interval cannot leave that range), which a threefold
error in clearance, in either direction, would not satisfy. The
troughs, and the accumulation over the week, are lower than in Figure S5: the
median concentration falls by about a factor of three between the first-dose
peak and 24 h in this implementation and by about a factor of two in the
figure. The typical extensive metabolizer reproduces the same faster decline,
so the gap is not a matter of the inter-individual variability. No
parameter in the Appendix S2 table, read as printed, closes it, and the
values were not adjusted.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Exposure driver.** The Methods define the Emax driver as the average
  steady-state active-moiety concentration Cav,ss = Dose / (CL/F x 28 days),
  computed per sampling occasion from the Laveille 2024 model; the control
  stream's `$INPUT` names the column `CONC`. The model takes it as the `CAV`
  covariate (0 for placebo). The drift term, which the control stream
  switches on with `IF(DOSE.NE.0)`, is switched on by `CAV > 0`; its random
  effect applies to every patient, as in the control stream.
- **Typical CAV in this vignette.** The cohorts use one CAV per arm (38.6
  ng/mL for 100 mg from the Discussion, scaled to 28.95 ng/mL for 75 mg)
  instead of individual post hoc values, which are not reported. Because
  EC50 (4.6 ng/mL) is far below both values, the PANSS predictions are
  insensitive to this.
- **Time constant TD.** Table 2 and the Results describe TD as the time to
  reach 68.3% of the maximal placebo effect. With the Weibull form, the
  fraction reached at t = TD is 1 - exp(-1) = 63.2% (the control-stream comment
  says 63%); the equation is implemented as printed.
- **Drug-effect onset half-life.** Table 2 and the control stream give KTHL in
  days (8.96 day); the Discussion's "~9 h" is read as days.
- **Dropout hazard sign.** Appendix S1 prints h(t) = BHAZ x exp(-predictor x
  beta) with positive estimates beta_PANSS = 0.049 and beta_USA = 0.996. Read
  literally, a typical patient (PANSS about 90) would have a hazard near
  1e-7 per day, so practically nobody would drop out, contradicting the
  stated purpose of the model (dropout depending on PANSS severity). The
  model therefore uses h = BHAZ x exp(0.049 x PANSS + 0.996 x USA): higher
  PANSS and US enrollment raise the hazard. PANSS enters uncentred and as the
  model-predicted individual score; the appendix does not say whether the
  observed or predicted score was used.
- **Country and injection site.** PRISMA-3 enrolled only in the USA and
  Ukraine, so the Ukraine effect on baseline is written with
  `1 - REGION_USA`. The deltoid indicator `INJSITE_ARM` is the source's
  `SINJ - 1`; the gluteal muscle is the reference.
- **IIV fixed to zero.** The control stream carries zero-fixed variances for
  POW and EC50; those random effects are omitted.
- **Oral model: CYP2D6 phenotype.** The source estimates the phenotype as a
  latent three-subpopulation mixture. The model selects the subpopulation
  through the indicators `CYP2D6_PM` and `CYP2D6_IM` (extensive metabolizer
  when both are 0); this vignette draws them with the mixture probabilities.
  The single logit-scale IIV of FP and the single IIV of CLPM are shared by the
  three subpopulations, as the table prints one value for each.
- **Oral model: IOV.** The occasion is not defined in the source. The model
  declares the inter-occasion random effects on F1, D1 and KA at the `OCC`
  level; this vignette draws a new value for every daily dose.
- **Oral model: active moiety.** The active moiety is the plain sum of the
  risperidone and 9-hydroxyrisperidone concentrations (no molecular-weight
  correction is mentioned), and amounts converted to 9-hydroxyrisperidone are
  carried in risperidone mass units.
- **Oral model: residual error.** Not reported (the simulations exclude it);
  the proportional residual errors are fixed to 0.
- **Oral model: trough discrepancy.** See the PKNCA section: the simulated
  troughs and steady-state peaks are lower than those read from Figure S5.
